docs_sample.description: Here's the complete broadcast of A CBS Special Movie Presentation of the made-for-TV film, "A Christmas Without Snow," as aired over WBBM Channel 2. This stars Michael Learned (seen also on "Nurse" here - https://youtu.be/Q_gTsaWxTs4) as a divorcee who moves from Omaha to San Francisco and becomes a member of a church choir around the holidays. Also features John Houseman, James Cromwell, and Valerie Curtin. Includes: Station ID / Bill Kurtis promoting "John Lennon focus report at 10" (all Lennon-related bumper and news updates were posted separately here: https://youtu.be/FHMkhzn-K4M) Show opening titles and film preview (posted separately here, including the complete first break: https://youtu.be/Ukp91JQBE5U) Commercials for: Sears (with reworking of "The Night Before Christmas") Theatrical trailer for "Stir Crazy" Shell Oil - offer for "The Energy Saving Book" Instant Quaker Oatmeal Film segment 1, starting with opening titles Commercials for: Clairol Total Skin Care System (and other Christmas gifts) Samsonite luggage ("Isn't that...? - Yes, it's Samsonite") High Point decaffeinated coffee Timex watches ("We're making time look good") Film segment 2 Commercials for: Stroh Light Beer Olympus OM-10 camera Speak & Spell - from Texas Instruments Pizza Hut's Pan Pizza "We will return" bumper Promo for "Mark, I Love You" for Wednesday (voiceover by ??) Promo for John Lennon: The Dream Is Over (voiceover by Bill Gilliand) CBS 'Eye-D' (voiceover by Lee Jordan) Commercials for: Kinney Boots - with Ken Berry Marshall Field's - with Oscar De La Renta (himself) Station ID - with Bill Kurtis previewing story on Poland's border for 10pm news Film segment 3 Commercials for: Mazola 100% Pure Corn Oil Hallmark Christmas Cards (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/GUtwm9XHXe0) Reynolds Wrap aluminum foil (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/b_5bbej3vrw) American Express Card - with Roberta Peters (voiceover by Peter Thomas) "We will return" bumper Promo for Bugs Bunny's Looney Christmas Tales and 'Twas the Night Before Christmas (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/PId4_2q-P_s) CBS 'Eye-D' (voiceover by Lee Jordan) Channel 2 Newsbreak with Bill Kurtis (opening voiceover by Jerry Harper), with stories: - Yoko Ono announces no funeral for John Lennon; a photo of Lennon signing autograph for his killer is shown - Mayor Byrne announces top brass will get pay raise Commercial: Wakefield Frozen Crab Bill ends Newsbreak with promo for THE 10 O'Clock News Station ID / promo for Rockford (voiceover by Jerry Harper) Film segment 4 Commercials for: Sears Classic Collection Sale (on tailored suits - ends December 13th) Taylor California Sellers Burgundy Wine (with Irena Chalmers) Vicks Sinex long-acting nasal spray New Come 'n' Get It 4-Flavor Dry Dog Food Film segment 5 Commercials for: Theatrical trailer for "Seems Like Old Times" (voiceover by Skip Hinnant?) Maxwell House coffee (with uber-busy telephone switchboard operator) Dristan Long Lasting Nasal Mist (with Liz Byrne given a Breathing Bag Test) (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/UVtTg5IEPno) Clairol Instant Hair Setter "We will return" bumper Promo for Magnum P.I. premiere, followed by Knots Landing, for Thursday Repeat of promo for John Lennon: The Dream Is Over CBS 'Eye-D' (voiceover by Lee Jordan) Commercials for: Chateau La Salle wine - from Christian Brothers of California Jōvan Musk Oil for men and women (ending voiceover by Jerry Harper) Station ID / Bill Kurtis promo for John Lennon remembrances for 10pm Film segment 6 Commercials for: The Cheryl Tiegs Collection from Sears Kellogg's - Merry Christmas (with Sugar Frosted Flakes' Tony the Tiger and Tony Jr.; Rice Krispies' Snap, Crackle and Pop; Cocoa Krispies' Tusk the elephant; Sugar Smacks' Dig 'Em the Frog; and Froot Loops' Toucan Sam) (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/Vq4v1rEq15E) Polaroid One-Step camera (Christmas-themed, with James Garner and Mariette Hartley) (posted separately here: https://youtu.be/6OYH5Jw2B6Q) 7th and final film segment, with ending credits afterward (and voiceover promo for John Lennon: The Dream Is Over by Lee Jordan) This aired on local Chicago TV on Tuesday, December 9th 1980 during the 8:00pm to 9:58pm timeframe. About The Museum of Classic Chicago Television: The MCCTv (FuzzyMemoriesTV) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit whose primary mission is the preservation and display of off-air, early home videotape recordings (70s to early 80s, mostly) recorded off of TV (in Chicago or other cities now too); things which would likely be lost if not sought out and preserved digitally. Even though (mostly) short clips are displayed here, we preserve the entire broadcasts in our archives - the complete programs with breaks, for historical preservation. For information on how to help in our mission, to donate or lend tapes to be converted to DVD, please e-mail tapes@fuzzy.tv Thank you for your help!

docs_sample.creator: WNYW-FOX Corporation; WCBS-Paramount Global; WNET-Public Broadcasting System; Classic Media; Sesame Workshop;
docs_sample.description: (c)1986 This DVD Transfer consists mostly of Christmas specials taped in the New York area around December 1986; but also contains part of a TBS ("SuperStation TBS", to be precise) recording of "King Kong vs. Godzilla" and a couple of partial Sesame Street episodes (acquired via eBay). Picture starts off rough in spots but improves by the time we get to "Rudolph's Shiny New Year". CONTENTS 1. Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (based on the later recordings being confirmed from WNYW-TV 5 - more details in the entry for "From All of Us to All of You" - this was apparently taped from WCBS-TV 2 in New York) 2. Nestor, the Long-Eared Christmas Donkey (may have been taped on WNYW-TV 5. The 1977 special based on the 1975 song penned by someone who knew a thing or two about Christmas songs in Gene Autry {alongside Dave Burgess and Don Pfrimmer} features the usual "celebrity narrator" pattern used in other Rankin-Bass specials - in this case country legend Roger Miller as the narrator Spieltoe {another donkey owned by Santa} alongside a cast including Eric Stern {as Nestor}; Brenda Vaccaro {whose notable roles included at that time co-starring alongside Jon Voight and Dustin Hoffman in 1969's "Midnight Cowboy" [which saw her nominated for a Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actress] and 1975's "Once is Not Enough" [winning the Golden Globe in the same category while also nominated for an Oscar]. In later years; Vaccaro's resume included voicing the mother of the title character in the late 1990s Cartoon Network cartoon "Johnny Bravo"; appearing in the role of Millicent Winter on stage for the play "Nice Work If You Can Get It" in August 2015 after Valerie Harper - already diagnosed with the brain cancer which ultimately claimed her life in 2019 - bowed out after falling unconscious in late July 2015 and most recently a guest spot in the HBO series "And Just Like That..." {a spinoff/sequel to "Sex and the City"}; legendary voice actor Paul Frees {whose roster of characters included Boris Badenov, Toucan Sam, Ludwig Von Drake and the Pillsbury Doughboy; Frees was also a Rankin-Bass regular whose most notable role with them was Burgermeister Meisterburger in 1970's "Santa Claus is Comin' to Town"}; Linda Gary {primarily a voice actress most associated with Filmation's projects}; Iris Rainer {who voiced the title character in 1971's "Here Comes Peter Cottontail" before shifting focus to writing, with her most notable work being the 1985 novel "Beaches" - eventually adapted into the 1988 movie starring Bette Midler and Barbara Hershey} and another legendary voice actor in Don Messick {most associated with Hanna-Barbera, where he voiced characters such as Astro, Muttley, Boo Boo Bear and Ranger Smith, Scooby-Doo and Papa Smurf. Probably his most well-known role for a studio outside of Hanna-Barbera was his late-career role as Hamton J. Pig in "Tiny Toon Adventures"}) 3. The Year Without a Santa Claus (voice-over at the end allowed me to confirm this aired on WNYW-TV 5; the flagship for the just-launched FOX network. The 1974 special features Shirley Booth as Mrs. Claus {serving both as narrator and principal character while Old St. Nick is under the weather; Booth - who won a Best Actress Oscar for her role as Lola Delaney in 1952's "Come Back, Little Sheba"{having won her 2nd of 3 Tony Awards for that same role in 1950} and later starring as the title character in the 1961-66 NBC/CBS sitcom "Hazel" {which netted 2 Emmy wins} - retired from acting after this project}; film legend Mickey Rooney as Santa Claus {Rooney's second time voicing Santa for a Rankin-Bass project; the first being 1970's "Santa Claus is Comin' to Town". Rooney would reprise the role twice more in 1979's "Rudolph and Frosty's Christmas in July" and once more in one of the final roles of Rooney's LONG career: 2008's "A Miser Brothers' Christmas". In between his first and second times voicing Santa, Rooney turned down a role that likely would have kick-started a stalled career: Archie Bunker in "All in the Family"}; Dick Shawn {a comedian and frequent "Tonight Show" substitute for Johnny Carson - with one of his being a TV trivia note as his appearance hosting the New Year's Day 1971 episode included the very last TV ad for a cigarette before cigarette ads were banned from the American airwaves}; George S. Irving {first of three appearances in Rankin-Bass productions; later voicing Geppetto in 1980's "Pinocchio's Christmas" and joining Mickey Rooney for 2008's "A Miser Brothers Christmas". Irving's best-known role is as the narrator {and Tap Tap the Chizzler} in the 1964-67 NBC/CBS cartoon "Underdog"; while the same year of this special's premiere [1974] Irving also won a Tony for his role alongside Debbie Reynolds and Jane Powell in the 1974 musical "Irene"}; Bob McFadden {whose voice roles ranged from the title character in commercials for Franken Berry cereal; Snarf from the 1980s cartoon "ThunderCats" and the really loud parrot yelling "Ring around the collar" in commercials for Wisk detergent} and Bradley Bolke {best known as the voice of Chumley the Walrus in the 1963-66 CBS cartoon "Tennessee Tuxedo and His Tales"}) 4. "From All of Us to All of You" (this was an "animated Christmas card" from Disney that first premiered in 1958 with hosting duties shared by Mickey Mouse, Jiminy Cricket, Tinker Bell and a "cricket-sized" Walt Disney himself {Walt and Tinker Bell's segments, along with 1932's "Santa's Workshop", were dropped in 1963 - with the space which had been held by the latter being replaced with teasers for upcoming films for a while} last appeared on network television in 1980 {when the Disney anthology series was in the last year of its first run on NBC} but remained at least through 1986 in syndication and the newly-launched Disney Channel before disappearing from American airwaves at an unknown date {though the special can be seen in other countries, being especially popular in Sweden}. Featured segments included 1949's "Toy Tinkers" {which is led into by an extended intro and Chip and Dale doing a song-and-dance routine} followed by a series of "Memorable Moments" {sort of a Disney animation highlight reel} featuring: "You Can Fly" {from 1953's "Peter Pan"}; a scene of Bambi and Thumper skating on ice {from 1942's "Bambi"}; "I've Got No Strings" {from 1940's "Pinocchio"}; "Bella Notte" {from 1955's "Lady and the Tramp"}; "The Work Song/A Dream is a Wish Your Heart Makes" {from 1950's "Cinderella"}; "The Silly Song" {from the film that started it all in terms of feature-length animated films - 1937's "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs"} plus a "surprise gift" in "Bare Necessities" AND "I Wanna Be Like You" {from 1967's "The Jungle Book"} before Jiminy closes things with "When You Wish Upon a Star") 5. "A Charlie Brown Christmas" (taped from WCBS-TV 2) 6. "King Kong vs. Godzilla" (about 48 minutes of the 1963 Americanized version of the 1962 Japanese film {with American cast members including Michael Keith, Harry Holcombe, James Yagi, Les Tremayne, Paul Mason and Bruce Howard either played new characters or providing voice-overs for the English dub} as recorded off what was SuperStation WTBS {now simply TBS})  7. "Sesame Street" (partial; sponsored by J, O and 8) 8. "Sesame Street" (missing intro; sponsored by I, K and 11 {don't recall seeing a double-digit number as a sponsor before} and includes the famous "Pinball Number Count" from 1 to 12 segment with vocals by the then-little known group The Pointer Sisters shortly before becoming one of the biggest R&B groups of the 1980s) 9. Planet Earth (a PBS series sponsored by the Annenberg/CPB Project and IBM; this episode deals with ocean exploration and was the last recording before the tape ran out)
docs_sample.title: DVD Transfer 161 (Mostly Christmas Specials Taped from December 1986)
